scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: Sarah is doing maintenance on a cabin panel. She feels well.
charm_assessment: Vital signs at her personal baseline.
immediate_action_steps: Continue work; wear gloves for panel work.
basis: Sarah's baseline from the medic team's scenarios.

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: A sharp panel edge cuts deep into her left forearm. Bright red blood pulses out and floats away as droplets.
key_measurements: Bleeding: active | HR 96 | BP 120/80 | RR 18 | SpO2 98% | Shock index 0.80
charm_assessment: Life-threatening bleeding: blood is pulsing from the wound. Vital signs are still normal (ATLS class I, under 15% of blood volume), but they will not stay normal. Act before they change.
checks_requested: Find the exact bleeding point; check that she is awake and talking.
blood_lab_tests: None now. Bleeding control comes first.
immediate_action_steps: Put on gloves and eye protection; Anchor Sarah and yourself with foot loops; Press gauze firmly on the wound with both hands; Call the crew: bleeding kit and tourniquet now
equipment: Gloves, eye protection, gauze, bleeding-control kit with tourniquet.
treatment_guidance: Bleeding control only. No medication is needed for this step.
basis: Stop the Bleed (American College of Surgeons): pulsing blood = life-threatening bleeding; apply pressure. ATLS class I: under 15% blood loss, HR under 100, normal BP.

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: Blood soaks through the gauze despite pressure. Sarah is anxious and breathing faster.
key_measurements: Bleeding: active | HR 112 | BP 116/88 | RR 22 | SpO2 98% | Shock index 0.97
charm_assessment: Bleeding continues despite pressure. Heart rate 100–120 with normal systolic pressure fits ATLS class II (15–30% of blood volume). A tourniquet is needed now.
checks_requested: Is blood still coming through the dressing?; Heart rate and blood pressure.
immediate_action_steps: Keep pressing while a crewmate opens the tourniquet; Pack the wound with hemostatic gauze if a tourniquet is delayed; Do not lift the dressing to look
equipment: Tourniquet, hemostatic gauze, BP monitor, pulse oximeter.
basis: Stop the Bleed: bleeding that continues despite pressure is life-threatening; pack the wound. ATLS class II: 15–30% loss, HR 100–120, normal systolic BP.

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: The tourniquet is placed above the wound and tightened. The bleeding stops.
key_measurements: Bleeding: controlled | HR 108 | BP 114/82 | RR 20 | SpO2 98% | Shock index 0.95
charm_assessment: Bleeding controlled. Heart rate over 100 and shock index above 0.9 show real blood loss (ATLS class II). Watch for shock.
checks_requested: Bleeding stopped?; Heart rate and blood pressure every 5 minutes; Awake and talking?
blood_lab_tests: Hemoglobin and hematocrit if an onboard analyzer is available (a first value may still look normal).
immediate_action_steps: Place the tourniquet 5–8 cm above the wound, not on a joint; Twist the windlass until the bleeding stops; Lock the windlass; Write down the time; Do not loosen it without the flight surgeon
equipment: Tourniquet, marker or tablet for the time, BP monitor, pulse oximeter, analyzer if available.
treatment_guidance: No medication decision by CHARM. Fluids only per the approved mission protocol.
basis: Stop the Bleed: tourniquet 2–3 inches above the wound, never on a joint, tighten until bleeding stops, note the time. Shock index above 0.9 is linked to worse outcomes.

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: The flight surgeon cannot answer in real time: the signal delay is too long.
key_measurements: Live values keep streaming to CHARM.
charm_assessment: CHARM keeps the onboard bleeding protocol and reassessment running until Earth answers. Loss of the link does not change the status.
immediate_action_steps: Follow the onboard bleeding protocol; Record every step with its time
equipment: CHARM tablet plus the same equipment.
treatment_guidance: Continue the plan already authorized for the mission.

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: Sarah rests, anchored. The tourniquet holds. She drinks small sips.
key_measurements: Bleeding: controlled | HR 98 | BP 116/78 | RR 18 | SpO2 98% | Shock index 0.84
charm_assessment: Heart rate back under 100 and shock index under 0.9: the circulation is coping. Still watch closely.
checks_requested: Heart rate and blood pressure every 15 minutes; Tourniquet time; Fingers below the tourniquet stay pale and cool (expected)
immediate_action_steps: Keep her warm and anchored; Small sips of fluid if she is fully awake and not nauseous; Check the tourniquet time every 15 minutes
equipment: BP monitor, pulse oximeter, blanket, fluid pouch.
treatment_guidance: Fluids only per the approved protocol. CHARM does not choose or dose fluids or drugs.
basis: ATLS class I–II range: HR under 100 with normal BP.

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: The flight surgeon answers with the plan for the wound and the tourniquet.
key_measurements: Bleeding: controlled | HR 86 | BP 118/76 | RR 16 | SpO2 98%
charm_assessment: Stable. Wound care and the tourniquet plan follow the flight surgeon's instructions.
checks_requested: Vital signs every 30 minutes; Dressing dry?
blood_lab_tests: Repeat hemoglobin per the flight surgeon.
immediate_action_steps: Follow the flight surgeon's wound plan; Document the tourniquet time and the wound care
treatment_guidance: Wound closure and any medication only on the flight surgeon's instructions.

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: The wound is dressed and Sarah is back on light duty.
key_measurements: Bleeding: none | HR 74 | BP 118/76 | RR 14 | SpO2 98%
charm_assessment: Back to her baseline. Keep watching the wound for infection.
blood_lab_tests: Hemoglobin follow-up if it was low.
immediate_action_steps: Return to light duty after clearance; Report fever, redness or swelling at once

scenario: Scenario 5: Severe bleeding from a deep cut (emergency)
what_happens: Sarah becomes pale, sweaty and confused; the pulse is fast and weak.
key_measurements: HR above 120 | Systolic BP falling (below 90) | RR above 30 | Shock index 1.0 or more
charm_assessment: Signs of ATLS class III shock (30–40% of blood volume). Treat as an emergency even if the bleeding looks controlled.
checks_requested: Look again for bleeding; Continuous HR, BP, SpO2.
immediate_action_steps: Lie her flat with legs raised and keep her warm; Oxygen if indicated by the protocol; Flight surgeon now
equipment: Oxygen, IV kit if trained, monitoring.
treatment_guidance: IV fluids only per the approved protocol.
basis: ATLS class III: 30–40% loss, HR 120–140, decreased BP. Shock index above 1 is linked to about four times the mortality.
